I couldn't write these notes, because none of my research worked. My first batch of searches hit the tool's usage limit before returning any results, and after that I wasn't allowed to make any more searches or open any pages.

That means I haven't read a single page from your approved sites. Your rules say to report only what those pages say and to cite a URL for every point, so I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would come from my own memory and couldn't be checked against a source.

If you start a new turn, I'll do the research again with fewer searches at once so it stays under the limit. I'd read the sources in this order:

1. **Main verse-by-verse sources:** the Enduring Word commentary on Habakkuk 3, the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com and studylight.org, and preceptaustin.org.
2. **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes, especially on "Shigionoth" (v. 1), Teman and Paran (v. 3), Cushan and Midian (v. 7), and the Hebrew of vv. 13–14.
3. **Where traditions differ:**
   - v. 2, "revive" (Wesleyan and revival readings versus Reformed ones)
   - v. 13, "Your anointed" (whether it refers to Christ, the king or Israel)
   - vv. 17–19, joy despite loss (set against prosperity teaching)
   - Lutheran, Catholic and Orthodox uses of this chapter, including its use as a canticle in church worship
4. **Sermons:** Spurgeon, Desiring God and Ligonier on vv. 17–19.

You could also send me page URLs you already trust from these sites. I can open those directly without searching first.
